newsitem.title: USA: Baxter, others seek added damages from CellPro.
newsitem.headline: Baxter, others seek added damages from CellPro.

text.p: Baxter International Inc, Becton Dickinson and Co and Johns Hopkins University jointly announced Tuesday they have filed motions seeking additional damages from CellPro Inc, which lost a patent infringement case last month.

The plaintiffs said they are seeking increased damages of $6.7 million and reimbursement of $7 million in litigation expenses. They also want a court-ordered transitional phase designed not to disrupt patients being treated by the CellPro product found to infringe on the two patents.
CellPro officials were not available for comment.
In March, a federal jury in Delaware found CellPro guilty of infringing on the plaintiff's patents on stem cell separation products associated with bone marrow transplants.
At the time, CellPro said it would appeal the $2.3-million jury award.

The latest filing would allow CellPro to continue selling its Ceprate SC Stem Cell Concentration System and its Ceprate LC34 Laboratory Cell Separation System to existing customers as the injunction takes effect in stages.
The systems are used to purify stem cells for bone marrow or peripheral blood transplantation, the companies said.
